icps.name: The TTC User
icps.persona: 28–35, actively trying to conceive 0–6 months, cycle-aware, often partnered.
icps.awareness_stage: Solution-aware (knows fertility apps exist, comparing options)
icps.search_behavior: Queries on accuracy, BBT, ovulation prediction, partner sharing, time-to-conceive stats.
ctas: Invite your partner to Flo for Partners

icps.name: The PCOS Patient
icps.persona: 22–40, recently diagnosed PCOS or suspects it; managing irregular cycles, weight, mood, skin.
icps.awareness_stage: Problem- or Solution-aware (knows symptoms, seeking management tools)
icps.search_behavior: Symptom-specific queries, diagnosis stories, app comparisons, telehealth platforms.
objections: General app vs dedicated PCOS app
ctas: Log your symptoms for your next appointment

icps.name: The Perimenopause User
icps.persona: 40–52, experiencing cycle changes, hot flashes, mood shifts, sleep disruption.
icps.search_behavior: Symptom validation, HRT info, app comparisons (Balance, Caria), Mayo Clinic-style authority.
objections: Flo is a period app, not menopause app
ctas: See what Flo + Mayo Clinic learned about perimenopause

icps.name: The Privacy-First User
icps.persona: Security-conscious, post-Roe context, often US-based or with cross-state legal concerns.
icps.awareness_stage: Problem-aware (knows period apps share data) or Solution-aware (evaluating private options)
icps.search_behavior: Queries Mozilla, Consumer Reports, Drip vs Euki vs Flo, ISO certifications, Anonymous Mode.

icps.name: The Teen / Young Adult
icps.persona: 16–22, first or early years of cycle tracking, often guided by friends or parents.
icps.awareness_stage: Problem-aware (just got their period) or Unaware (lifestyle drift to tracking)
icps.search_behavior: Queries are simple and emotional: 'is my period normal', 'best app for teens', 'is Flo safe'.
ctas: Track your first cycles with Flo
What's normal for periods at your age
